**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blocking finding. This is a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut.

Review record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4360#issuecomment-7218512109

## Scope and tier

- The PR adds one kernel (`RadialDrop`) with its tests and one decision file. Nothing calls the kernel.
- The diff against `upstream/main` has 4 files and 526 added lines. It removes no line.
- No posted G-code, golden, catalog program, UI file, dependency or process file changes.
- The kernel is contact geometry that a later slice will use for a gouge-free path. I reviewed it at the SAFETY tier.

## What looks good

- The law is correct. A facet grown by the ball is convex, so its contact interval on the ray has one top end. Each candidate (vertex sphere, edge cylinder with the foot on the edge, face offset with the foot in the triangle) is a point at distance `r` from the facet. Thus no candidate is above the true top, and the true top is one of them.
- The two culls are conservative. The axial bins grow each facet span by `r` (`radial_drop.rs:123`). The sphere test adds `r` to the reach (`radial_drop.rs:159`).
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` is in the kernel. `bin_of` clamps each index (`radial_drop.rs:172-175`). The bin count has a cap of 4096.
- Bad input is refused by name: the radius, an empty mesh, a corner that is not finite, an axis that is not a direction.
- A degenerate facet does not crash. Its edges and corners still give the contact.
- No contact gives `None`. The kernel does not invent a radius.
- The module has its provenance text. The files have 241 and 236 lines.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line, the mutation table, "Goldens moved: none" and ends with `Refs #2772` (partial work). The commit subject is conventional.
- `docs/decisions/2772-radial-drop.md` records the choice, the reason and the dropped options.

## Mutations that I ran again

I changed the kernel in my worktree, ran the pins, and restored the file each time.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| M6: sphere cull without `+ self.r` (`radial_drop.rs:159`) | red: `the_screw_rotor_drop_touches_and_never_gouges` |
| M8: axial bins without the `r` padding (`radial_drop.rs:123`) | red: `a_facet_reaches_every_station_within_the_ball_radius` |
| M4: edge foot not checked against the segment (`radial_drop.rs:213`) | red: vertex, screw and march pins |

Restored: 9 of 9 pass. `git status` is clean.

## An independent check

I added a temporary test in my worktree and removed it after the run. It is not in the PR.

- 40 random meshes of 32 facets each. Each mesh has one facet with collinear corners and one facet that is a point.
- The axis is tilted, does not go through the origin, and its direction is not a unit vector.
- 1600 queries: 706 gave a contact and 894 gave `None`.
- At each contact the nearest distance to the mesh is `r` within 1e-7. No centre of 400 samples farther out is nearer than `r`.
- At each `None`, no centre of 6001 samples on the full line is nearer than `r`.
- The test passed. It also failed under each of the three mutations above, so it can see a defect.

## Goldens

None moved. `git diff --stat upstream/main` shows only the 4 files of this PR.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Notes for the wiring slice (not blocking)

1. `centre_radius` reads the full line, not only the outer half. In my random check, 236 of 706 contacts had a negative radius: the only facets near the ray were across the axis. The module text says that the caller judges a contact below `r` (`radial_drop.rs:23-25`). The wiring slice must refuse or handle such a station, and pin it with a test.
2. The cull is weak for long axial facets. Each facet is put in each bin that its span covers (`radial_drop.rs:121-127`), and the bounding sphere of a long thin facet has a large reach. A mesh with many facets along the full length (an extruded profile) makes large bin lists and tests most facets for each query. Measure the time and the memory on the reporter's 1.15 M-facet mesh before an operation uses the kernel.
3. Each contact pin uses world X through the origin. A pin with a tilted axis that is off the origin would keep the frame math pinned in the tree. My temporary check covered it for this head.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
